review_output: {"summary":"I found no BLOCKER, MAJOR or MINOR defects in the local, inactive vercel-native implementation in the supplied revision. This review covers local scope only. It does not certify test results, WP11 acceptance or remote enablement. Remote verification is still incomplete (second egress, real remote limiter, project override resistance), so this review does not authorize deployment enablement. What I checked: (1) Config gating. vercel-native is selected only when the deployment source is vercel, the topology is direct-vercel, VERCEL=1, VERCEL_ENV=preview, the expected project ID is non-empty and matches VERCEL_PROJECT_ID, and RATE_LIMIT_PROVIDER is exactly upstash_redis. Nothing is inferred from the provider. checkRateLimit rechecks this full gate against process.env on every request, plus getRateLimitProviderId(). So a cached or caller-supplied native config cannot skip the gate, and request headers cannot affect it. (2) Branch isolation. The native path reads only x-vercel-forwarded-for, and rateLimitRequestWithIdentity removes the forged cf-connecting-ip, x-real-ip and x-forwarded-for headers (the tests check this). The native key namespace is entry-vercel-native:, so it does not share buckets with the old modes. The old proof-mode branches are unchanged. (3) IP bucket normalization. canonicalizeIp returns IPv6 as compressed hex with no dotted tail and no repeated '::'. That makes the '::' expansion in nativeBucketIdentity well-defined, including the '::' and full 8-group edge cases. IPv4-mapped addresses fold into their IPv4 bucket. Zone IDs, ports, lists, empty values and over-length values are rejected (503) before the limiter is called. (4) Provider failure. A bad gate or missing IP returns 503 with Retry-After and no-store, and there is no memory or WAF fallback. The real-limiter test confirms that a missing or empty Upstash URL or token gives 503 with zero fetch calls, and that a network failure gives 503 after exactly one fetch. (5) Accepted residuals, unchanged. The /64 bucket policy allows rotation across /48 to /56 allocations. IPv4-compatible addresses and NAT64 traffic share low or deterministic buckets. 6to4 (2002::/16) and Teredo prefixes behave like other operator-allocated prefixes under the same /64 policy (a single IPv4 owner can rotate across many /64 buckets). The project/runtime check is an operator configuration guard, not attestation.
